finding.title: Automate hooks/pre-commit installation instead of relying on manual copy/chmod instructions
finding.why: The pre-commit hook only runs if a contributor manually copies it into .git/hooks/ — there is no `make install-hooks`/`setup` target anywhere in either Makefile that does this for them, confirmed by grepping both Makefiles for 'hook' and finding no match. This repo's own `.git/hooks/pre-commit` is absent right now, empirically confirming the gate is not installed even in the reference checkout. CI backstops the same two checks (format/analyze), so this is not a silent-corruption risk, but it means every new contributor's first several commits get zero local pre-commit feedback and the guardrail is bypassable by simply never running the two setup lines — exactly the 'check that can never fire by default' pattern this audit area was asked to hunt.
finding.recommendation: Add a `make install-hooks` target (or a postinstall step referenced from the top-level setup docs) that performs the cp+chmod, and reference it from hooks/README.md/CONTRIBUTING.md instead of raw shell steps.
acceptance_criteria: A committed make/tool target installs hooks/pre-commit into .git/hooks/ without manual copy-paste.
hooks/README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, learning_tracker/README.md, and docs/development-guide.md point to that target.

finding.title: Anchor no_raw_logevent's analytics_service.dart whitelist check to its directory, not just filename
finding.why: Every sibling rule anchors its 'authorised owner' exemption to a directory path (lib/core/theme/, lib/core/labels/, lib/core/auth/, lib/core/sync/, lib/core/logging/) — no_raw_logevent is the only one that matches by bare filename suffix. Today there is exactly one file named analytics_service.dart (lib/core/analytics/analytics_service.dart), so this is latent, not live, but any future file anywhere in the tree named exactly analytics_service.dart (a copy, a per-feature override, a rewrite-in-progress) automatically inherits the exemption and can call raw logEvent() unchecked, silently defeating the rule's purpose of forcing typed AnalyticsEvent helpers (PV-5 territory).
finding.recommendation: Change the check to `path.endsWith('core/analytics/analytics_service.dart')` (or `path.contains('lib/core/analytics/')`) to match the directory-anchored pattern used by every other rule in this package.
acceptance_criteria: no_raw_logevent.dart's _isWhitelisted requires the core/analytics/ directory segment, not just the filename.
A regression test asserts a decoy lib/features/x/analytics_service.dart is NOT whitelisted (depends on the missing test file being added per the companion finding).

finding.title: Document all 9 shipped custom_lint rules in README.md; fix the 'eight rules' miscount
finding.why: learning_tracker_lints.dart's doc comment claims 'eight rules' but lists and registers nine (NoColorLiteralOutsideTheme, NoCurriculumDisplayNameBypass, NoEToStringInUi, NoFeatureCrossImport, NoFirebaseOutsideCore, NoHardcodedDomainTerm, NoHardcodedTextDirection, NoRawLogEvent, NoRawTalker). README.md documents only 5 (Rules 1-5: curriculum-bypass, feature-cross-import, firebase-outside-core, raw-talker, hardcoded-text-direction) and its 'Configuration' disable-list matches only those 5. Verified via git log that no_color_literal_outside_theme (0c66c611), no_hardcoded_domain_term (e84e880f), and no_e_to_string_in_ui + no_raw_logevent (bc327fef) were each added in commits that never touched README.md — the doc was last updated in a56ac75b, before any of those three commits. A developer hitting one of the 4 undocumented rules gets no 'why it exists'/'how to fix' guidance the other 5 rules provide.
finding.recommendation: Add README.md sections for no_color_literal_outside_theme, no_hardcoded_domain_term, no_e_to_string_in_ui, and no_raw_logevent (same What/Why/How-to-fix format as Rules 1-5), extend the Configuration disable-list to all 9, and fix the doc-comment count.
acceptance_criteria: packages/custom_lints/README.md documents all 9 rules registered in learning_tracker_lints.dart.
learning_tracker_lints.dart's doc comment count matches the actual list length.

finding.title: Extend the Makefile RTL audit grep to cover Alignment.centerLeft/Right and TextAlign.left/right, not just EdgeInsets.only
finding.why: This is distinct from the already-baselined 'RTL grep only in root Makefile' duplication gap: even within the root Makefile's own RTL check [10/12], the pattern only matches `EdgeInsets\.only([^)]*\(left\|right\):` — it has no pattern for `Alignment.centerLeft/centerRight` or `TextAlign.left/right` at all (confirmed: zero hits for 'centerLeft', 'centerRight', or 'TextAlign' anywhere in either Makefile). Those two categories are exactly what no_hardcoded_text_direction.dart also bans, but since custom_lint is broken (baselined) and the Makefile grep never covered them either, hardcoded Alignment.centerLeft/Right or TextAlign.left/right usage in an RTL (Hebrew) app has NO functioning enforcement path today, not even the degraded one that exists for EdgeInsets.only.
finding.recommendation: Add `Alignment\.(centerLeft|centerRight)` and `TextAlign\.(left|right)` patterns to Makefile check [10/12] so the backstop has parity with the (currently broken) custom_lint rule's scope.
acceptance_criteria: Makefile RTL check greps for Alignment.centerLeft/centerRight and TextAlign.left/right in addition to EdgeInsets.only(left:/right:).
A deliberately introduced Alignment.centerLeft usage makes `make audit` fail.

finding.title: Fail fast on missing key.properties instead of silently debug-signing release Android builds (build.gradle.kts)
finding.rule: Tier-2 area note (security) — AG-11-adjacent CI guardrail soft-skip
finding.why: When KEYSTORE_BASE64 is unset (misconfigured secret, or a maintainer manually dispatches the 'Build APK' workflow with build_type=release before secrets are wired up), build.yml prints a warning but does not fail — it proceeds to 'flutter build apk --release'. Because key.properties was never written, Gradle's fallback here silently signs the 'release' APK with the shared, publicly-known Flutter debug keystore, then uploads it as a GitHub Actions artifact literally named learning-tracker-release-apk. Anyone who installs that artifact believing it's a genuine release build gets a debug-signed binary; since the debug key is identical across virtually all Flutter/Android-Studio installs, another developer's debug-signed build could later 'update' over it without Android's signature check objecting.
finding.recommendation: Make the release signingConfig fail fast (e.g. error("release build requested but key.properties is missing")) instead of silently substituting debug signing, or at minimum have build.yml's keystore-decode step exit 1 when build_type == 'release' and the secret is empty instead of only warning.
acceptance_criteria: flutter build apk --release (or ./gradlew assembleRelease) fails loudly when key.properties/keystore secret is absent, instead of producing a debug-signed 'release' artifact.
build.yml's release job aborts (non-zero exit) when KEYSTORE_BASE64 is empty and build_type=release.
